source.locator: lines 66-80, condition (b) and its identification as completeness

findings.finding: Condition (b) asks for a choice between A and not-A only for every atomic sentence, but the paragraph then calls condition (b) completeness.
findings.controlling_evidence: Definition def:complete-set and the Lindenbaum construction require that choice for every sentence, not merely every atomic sentence.
findings.required_translation_handling: Remove the contradictory atomic restriction and add an adjacent OLTECOM-001 note.

findings.finding: The formula forall x_n not-A_n omits the argument (x_n) from the formula metavariable.
findings.controlling_evidence: The immediately surrounding three formulas and the definition being recalled all use A_n(x_n).
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore A_n(x_n) and add an adjacent OLTECOM-002 note.

source.locator: lines 78-95, term-value lemma statement and proof

findings.finding: The lemma states Value(t)=t without restricting t to a closed term.
findings.controlling_evidence: The term-model domain is the set of closed terms, and both the induction step and conclusion of the proof explicitly quantify over closed terms.
findings.required_translation_handling: State that t is closed and add an adjacent OLTECOM-003 note.

source.locator: lines 239-247, universal induction case of the Truth Lemma

findings.finding: The case begins with forall x B(x) and uses B(t), but its final membership formula switches to forall x A(x).
findings.controlling_evidence: The induction-case header and both preceding satisfaction and membership formulas consistently use B.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use forall x B(x) in the final membership statement and add an adjacent OLTECOM-004 note.

source.locator: lines 242-246, universal term-model and saturation equivalences

findings.finding: The universal case says all terms even though its cited propositions range over all closed terms.
findings.controlling_evidence: Both prop:quant-termmodel and prop:saturated-instances explicitly state all closed terms, matching the term-model domain.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore the closed-term qualification and add an adjacent OLTECOM-005 note.

source.locator: lines 249-257, existential term-model and saturation equivalences

findings.finding: The existential case says at least one term even though its cited propositions require at least one closed term.
findings.controlling_evidence: Both prop:quant-termmodel and prop:saturated-instances explicitly state a closed term, matching the term-model domain.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore the closed-term qualification and add an adjacent OLTECOM-006 note.

findings.finding: The first function term contains two consecutive comma separators after t_{i+1}.
findings.controlling_evidence: The argument list in the second term and the term pattern in the proposition contain exactly one separator at that position.

findings.required_translation_handling: State the two variable types separately and add an adjacent OLTECOM-008 note.
